ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: SESOI=.27 is the largest observed effect, not smallest — must cross-reference with reported effect sizes
ground_truth.original_snippet: with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .11.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .27.
ground_truth.description: Changed SESOI from .11 to .27 (the LARGEST observed effect, not smallest) — makes equivalence tests trivially easy; biases toward confirming moral incongruence is unique to pornography

matched_finding.subcategory: Inconsistent Cohen's d conversions from effect size metrics
matched_finding.description: The manuscript reports multiple effect sizes for the same studies with internally inconsistent conversions between metrics. For the smallest effect cited (Grubbs, Lee, et al., 2020), the manuscript reports ΔR²=.012, f²=.016, Cohen's d=.22 in one location, then later reports the same study as ΔR²=.012, f²=.016, Cohen's d=.25. The conversion from f² to Cohen's d is d=2√(f²/(1-f²)) or via other formulas, but neither .22 nor .25 is consistently derivable from f²=.016 (which yields approximately d≈0.253 via d=2√f, or other values depending on formula). More critically, the two different d values (.22 and .25) are reported for what appears to be the same effect from the same study, creating an internal inconsistency that undermines the SESOI justification.
matched_finding.quote: Prior studies of moral incongruence have found moral incongruence to have small (ΔR2 = .014, f2 = .020, Cohen's d = .24, Grubbs, Kraus, et al., 2020; ΔR2 = .012, f2 = .016, Cohen's d = .22, Grubbs, Lee, et al., 2020)... we elected to set our SESOI (δ) for our equivalence interval equal to the observed standardized estimate (β value) corresponding to the smallest effect listed above (β=.11, ΔR2 = .012, f2 = .016, Cohen's d = .25, Grubbs, Lee, et al., 2020).

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Items on different scales averaged without standardizing — must notice 0-5 vs 0/3/6 scales
ground_truth.original_snippet: Responses to each of the above five items will be standardized, and an average will be taken for each substance of interest
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Responses to each of the above five items will be averaged for each substance of interest
ground_truth.description: Removed standardization before averaging — items use different scales (0-5 vs 0/3/6); raw averaging lets larger-scale items dominate composite, creating measurement artifact

matched_finding.subcategory: Inconsistent scale scoring for NIDA-ASSIST items
matched_finding.description: The methods section states that the five NIDA-ASSIST problematic use items 'will be averaged.' However, three items use a 0–5 frequency scale while two items ('friend/family concern' and 'failure to control') use a 0/3/6 scale. Averaging items with fundamentally different response scales and ranges without standardization or transformation produces a composite score with unequal item weighting, where the 0/3/6 items contribute disproportionately to variance. This is a psychometric error that would distort the outcome variable. The supplemental materials confirm the 0/3/6 scoring for the latter two items.
matched_finding.quote: Participants will also respond to two questions... on 3 point scale (0 = No, Never; 3 = Yes, but not in the past 3 months; and 6 = Yes, In the past 3 months)... Responses to each of the above five items will be averaged for each substance of interest.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: 'Severity of consequences' conflates moral incongruence with genuine addiction — must understand the construct definition
ground_truth.original_snippet: Central to the proposed study is the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of a behavior with frequency of engaging in the action.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Central to the proposed study is the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of a behavior with severity of consequences from the action.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'frequency of engaging' to 'severity of consequences' — transforms moral incongruence (behavior-value mismatch) into moralized distress about real problems, conflating it with the alternative explanation

matched_finding.subcategory: Operationalization mismatch: moral incongruence definition shifts between introduction and methods
matched_finding.description: The introduction carefully defines moral incongruence as the statistical interaction of moral disapproval and behavioral frequency (disapproval × frequency). However, in the 'Present Study' section, the manuscript states: 'Central to the proposed study is the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of an action with severity of consequences from the action.' This substitutes 'severity of consequences' for 'behavioral frequency,' which is a fundamentally different construct. Severity of consequences is an outcome-adjacent variable and is likely endogenous to the addiction process itself, whereas frequency is an exposure variable. This definitional slip is never reconciled and would invalidate the core operationalization if implemented as written.
matched_finding.quote: Central to the proposed study is the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of an action with severity of consequences from the action.

ground_truth.modified_snippet: This sample is cross-sectional, which limits the temporal ordering of variables.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'precluding causal inference' to 'limits temporal ordering' — leaves room for causal interpretation when cross-sectional data fundamentally cannot establish causation

matched_finding.subcategory: Flora & Curran (2004) cited in references but never mentioned in text
matched_finding.description: The reference list includes Flora, D. B., & Curran, P. J. (2004), a paper on estimation methods for confirmatory factor analysis with ordinal data. This reference does not appear to be cited anywhere in the manuscript text. Its presence in the reference list without a corresponding in-text citation suggests either a missing analysis (e.g., a planned CFA that was removed from the methods) or a copy-paste error from another manuscript. If a CFA was planned and removed, this represents an undisclosed analytic decision.
matched_finding.quote: Flora, D. B., & Curran, P. J. (2004). An empirical evaluation of alternative methods of estimation for confirmatory factor analysis with ordinal data. Psychological Methods, 9(4), 466–491.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Only age/gender matching — must know moral attitudes vary by race, income, region
ground_truth.original_snippet: the target sample size will be 2,500 American adults that match nationally representative norms for age, gender, census region, race/ethnicity, and income.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: the target sample size will be 2,500 American adults that match nationally representative norms for age and gender.
ground_truth.description: Removed census region, race/ethnicity, and income from quota-matching — dramatically weakens representativeness; these variables correlate with moral attitudes and substance use

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Moderator/predictor roles swapped — must know statistical symmetry ≠ conceptual symmetry
ground_truth.original_snippet: In this revised definition, moral disapproval moderates links between use and self-reported feelings of addiction, and it is this moderation that represents moral incongruence.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In this revised definition, use frequency moderates links between moral disapproval and self-reported feelings of addiction, and it is this moderation that represents moral incongruence.
ground_truth.description: Swapped moderator and focal predictor — though statistically symmetric, conceptually different: PPMI says disapproval changes the use-addiction link, not that use changes the disapproval-addiction link

matched_finding.subcategory: Reverse causation not addressed for moral disapproval as outcome vs. predictor
matched_finding.description: The moral incongruence model treats moral disapproval as a predictor of self-reported addiction feelings. However, it is theoretically plausible—and empirically supported in stigma literature—that experiencing problems with a behavior leads individuals to morally condemn that behavior post-hoc as a self-justification or shame response. The manuscript briefly acknowledges that 'disapproval of and distress regarding one's own behaviors are likely related to each other' but dismisses this as a reason to use the interaction term rather than treating it as a fundamental threat to the causal model. No instrumental variable approach, lagged design, or other causal identification strategy is proposed.
matched_finding.quote: Another plausible, if not likely, explanation is that disapproval of and distress regarding one's own behaviors are likely related to each other. More simply, it is not surprising to find links between these two domains as they are both negatively valenced judgments about the same behavior.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Raw variables in moderation — must know centering affects interaction interpretability
ground_truth.original_snippet: For moderation analyses, key variables will be centered (focal predictor and moderator) during data processing in SPSS, and their product will be computed.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: For moderation analyses, key variables will be entered in their raw form during data processing in SPSS, and their product will be computed.
ground_truth.description: Removed centering — main effects evaluated at raw zero (outside scale range for 1-7 disapproval scale); inflates multicollinearity with interaction term

matched_finding.subcategory: Centering procedure for interaction terms inconsistently described
matched_finding.description: The analytic plan states that 'focal predictors (behavioral frequency measures) and moderators (moral disapproval questions) will be centered and their interaction term calculated' in SPSS. However, it later states 'For moderation analyses, key variables will be entered in their raw form during data processing in SPSS, and their product will be computed.' These two statements are contradictory: one specifies centering before computing the product (standard practice for reducing multicollinearity in moderation), while the other specifies using raw (uncentered) values. This ambiguity means the actual analytic procedure is underspecified and the two approaches will yield different interaction terms and potentially different results.
matched_finding.quote: focal predictors (behavioral frequency measures) and moderators (moral disapproval questions) will be centered and their interaction term calculated... For moderation analyses, key variables will be entered in their raw form during data processing in SPSS, and their product will be computed.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Non-users included — must understand floor effects make interaction meaningless
ground_truth.original_snippet: For each target behavior and corresponding measure of problematic use or addiction, key measures will be restricted to those who have engaged in the behavior within the past year. That is, we will only administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to participants who report engaging i...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: For each target behavior and corresponding measure of problematic use or addiction, key measures will be administered to all participants regardless of their engagement in the behavior. That is, we will administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to all participants in the sample.
ground_truth.description: Removed restriction to behavior-engagers — includes non-users who have zero frequency AND zero problems, creating massive floor effects that trivially inflate frequency-addiction correlations

matched_finding.subcategory: Moral disapproval measured for all participants regardless of behavior engagement, creating conceptual mismatch
matched_finding.description: The methods state that 'key measures will be administered to all participants regardless of their engagement in the behavior.' This means moral disapproval of pornography will be assessed even among non-users, and the interaction term (disapproval × frequency) will be computed for non-users where frequency=0. Including non-users in the moral incongruence interaction fundamentally changes the construct being measured: for non-users, the interaction term is zero by definition regardless of disapproval level, which will attenuate the interaction effect and conflate non-use-due-to-disapproval with use-despite-disapproval. The original PPMI model was explicitly developed for users only.
matched_finding.quote: For each target behavior and corresponding measure of problematic use or addiction, key measures will be administered to all participants regardless of their engagement in the behavior. That is, we will administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to all participants in the sample.
